sections.h2: How is Athens-Clarke County property tax organized?
sections.html:
Clarke County and the City of Athens operate as one government, so the Athens-Clarke County Property Tax Division handles the bill for the whole county. Its page explains that the money supports the Clarke County Board of Education, Athens-Clarke County and the State of Georgia.

Real estate and business personal property taxes are generally due by October 20. If a bill goes unpaid, the property can be levied on and eventually sold. The division describes a 5% penalty added every 120 days past the due date, up to four times, for a possible total of 20%, on top of interest.

  • Land and buildings are taxed where they are located, per O.C.G.A. 48-5-11.
  • Taxable value is set at 40% of market value, with exceptions written into law (O.C.G.A. 48-5-7).
  • Standing timber escapes tax until it is sold or cut, then it is taxed at 100% of its fair market value.

Each bill shows both the fair market value and the assessed value, so you can see what the assessors used before you decide whether to appeal.

sections.h2: What sets Clarke County apart from the rest of Georgia?
sections.html:
Clarke is Georgia's smallest county by area, at 121 square miles including 1.8 of water. It lies in the Piedmont and drains mostly to the Upper Oconee River. The General Assembly carved it out of Jackson County on December 5, 1801 and named it for Elijah Clarke. Watkinsville served as seat until November 1871, when county offices moved to Athens. Athens and Winterville are the cities, and the town of Bogart lies mostly in Oconee County.

Its mills and railroad, which reached Athens in 1841, made it second only to Savannah and Chatham County in manufacturing investment during the 1840s. Today the University of Georgia shapes the housing market. Census QuickFacts counts 129,921 people for 2025, just 1.0% above the 2020 base, and households average 2.19 people with 16.1% of residents under 18.

Just 41.4% of homes are lived in by their owners, the lowest share among the four Georgia counties compared on QuickFacts, and typical rent is $1,219. An owner-held home has a middle value of $298,900, the middle household income is $53,625, and 73.5% of people stayed at the same address over the prior year. Many Athens houses are therefore rentals, and investor-owned homes receive the same bill as any other.

sections.h2: What are the steps to contest an Athens-Clarke County value?
sections.html:
Put the appeal in writing to the Board of Assessors, with 45 days counted from the mailing of the assessment notice. If the assessors leave the value alone, the file moves to the Board of Equalization on its own. The Athens-Clarke assessors answer questions at 706-613-3140.

Appeal timeline posted by Athens-Clarke County and the Georgia Department of Revenue
StepTiming
Written appeal delivered to the assessors45 days from notice mailing
Board of Equalization notifies both sides of hearing date15 days after the appeal reaches that board
Hearing held20 to 30 days after that letter
Appeal to Superior CourtWritten, 30 days after the Board of Equalization rules

At the hearing the Board of Assessors' appraiser presents comparable sales first, then you present your evidence, the Board of Equalization asks questions, and a ruling is sent to both sides. Arbitration and a hearing officer are the other two methods the state allows, and the assessors' office can explain them.

sections.h2: Which returns must Athens-Clarke County owners file?
sections.html:
Form PT-50R, the real estate return, goes to the tax commissioner in room 250 of the Courthouse before the April 1 close of the filing season, in any year the property was acquired or altered. If nothing affecting value has changed since last year, you may skip it. A taxpayer who fails to file a required return faces a 10% penalty on the value not returned, plus interest and possibly other penalties.

Personal property follows a stricter rule. Form PT-50P goes to the Board of Assessors every April 1 whether or not anything changed. The tax commissioner also warns buyers of businesses, boats and aircraft to check for unpaid personal property tax before closing, since attorneys usually search real estate taxes only.

sections.h2: What exemptions and refunds exist for Athens-Clarke County owners?
sections.html:
Georgia's state homestead exemption goes to people who own and occupy a home as their primary residence, and the Department of Revenue's page for Clarke County confirms that an application can be made at any time but must be in by April 1 of the first year the exemption is sought. Failing to apply counts as a waiver. Some counties add larger local exemptions, so ask the Athens-Clarke County offices which ones apply to a given house before you assume the standard amount is all there is.

Taxpayers can also ask in writing for a refund of tax that was erroneously or illegally assessed and collected, as long as the request starts within three years of payment. When an assessment is under appeal and the final taxable value comes in lower, the refund is processed automatically once that value is final. Equipment, machinery and fixtures used by a business are assessed at 40% of fair market value, and the assessor may value a going business as a whole.

sections.h2: What happens if taxes go unpaid in Athens-Clarke County?
sections.html:
Athens-Clarke County runs its own tax sales. The tax commissioner serves as ex officio sheriff, and Georgia law requires the property to be advertised for four consecutive weeks in the legal section of the county newspaper, which the county identifies as the Athens Banner-Herald.

  • Sales begin at 10:00 a.m. on the first Tuesday of the month, ordinarily in front of the courthouse, and run as a public outcry auction.
  • The opening bid equals the taxes due plus costs, and the property goes to the highest bidder or may be bid in for the county.
  • Payment is due at the sale, by cashier's or certified check from an FDIC-insured institution.
  • The tax commissioner then executes and records a tax deed. The purchaser owes taxes as they come due, and any amount paid may be added to the redemption price.

An owner who sees a notice for their address should contact the tax commissioner at once. Redemption rights exist under Georgia law, and the county's tax sale page has the current list of properties.

sections.h2: What should I settle at closing when selling in Clarke County?
sections.html:
Tax for the full year falls on the person who held title in January, and Georgia refunds nothing for months after a sale. Any credit for the stretch a buyer will own the home is worked out between the parties on the closing statement.

State guidance also gives taxpayers 60 days from the bill's postmark before interest starts. When the October 20 date has gone by with a balance still open, request a payoff figure with penalties included and pay it out of sale proceeds so the title is clear.

Rental owners selling an occupied house should confirm that business personal property, such as appliances listed on a business return, has no balance. Questions about exemptions, returns or values go to the assessors, and bills and payments go to the Property Tax Division.

faqs.q: What is the Athens-Clarke County due date?
faqs.a: October 20 in the usual case. The Property Tax Division lists that date for real estate and business personal property.

faqs.q: What is the Athens-Clarke County appeal window?
faqs.a: It is 45 days from the day the assessment notice was mailed. Send the appeal in writing to the Board of Assessors, and call 706-613-3140 with questions.

faqs.q: Who conducts tax sales in Clarke County?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner, acting as ex officio sheriff. Auctions start at 10:00 a.m. on each month's first Tuesday, usually in front of the courthouse.

faqs.q: Must I file a property return every year in Athens-Clarke County?
faqs.a: Not for real estate if nothing changed. Real estate returns are due January 1 to April 1 in years the property changed or was acquired, while personal property returns are due every April 1.

faqs.q: Do most Clarke County residents own their homes?
faqs.a: No. QuickFacts shows owners living in 41.4% of homes for 2020 to 2024, so renters are the majority.
